matches.commentary: First day of kindergarten. That first-handshake energy. We posted 95 points, which sounds like a confident opener until you discover that Justin Fields — owned, rostered, breathing — sat on the bench accumulating 31.52 points in complete, magnificent anonymity while Drake Maye started and scored 17.28. Xavier Worthy caught the ball zero times for zero points. Kenneth Walker totalled 3.90 in what the committee will formally log as the Kenneth Walker Opening Statement. We won 95–88. The committee convened. The committee drank.
matches.decision: Started Drake Maye (17.28 pts) with Justin Fields watching from the bench — where he scored 31.52. Xavier Worthy played himself into the phantom zone with a goose egg. Kenneth Walker contributed 3.90 in the FLEX spot. The Drawer opens.

matches.commentary: Amon-Ra St. Brown decided Week 2 was his spiritual awakening and scored 34.70 with the energy of a man who has just discovered his purpose. Brandon Aubrey — the kicker, the literal kicker — was our second-highest scorer at 24.50. The kicker. We also benched Dak Prescott (26.14) in favour of Justin Fields, who produced 3.98 points, which is marginally less than the value of one medium field goal. We are winning. Something is categorically wrong. The committee is investigating the wrong thing.
matches.decision: Started Justin Fields (3.98 pts) over Dak Prescott (26.14). This decision — scoring fewer points than our kicker's personal best — is what happens when management prioritises upside over arithmetic. Brandon Aubrey K finished second on the team. The Fields Drawer is now a documented location.

matches.commentary: The Inquiry. By official record, this match ended 131.86–131.84. The margin: 0.02 points. Two one-hundredths of a point. The cause of death: Drake Maye, actual starting-calibre quarterback, was sitting on the bench producing 23.22 fantasy points while we started a configuration of running backs that collectively couldn't close the gap. Had any single decision gone differently — any of them — this would have been a 20-point win. dpol did not win this match. The universe gave it to them. The investigation remains permanently open.
matches.decision: Drake Maye benched for 23.22 points. Started four running backs instead of the QB who was outscoring our entire active lineup from the reserve. The 0.02 is not a result. It is a debt. It is recorded.

matches.commentary: We scored 140. One hundred and forty points. Against a normal human opponent this is a decisive, emphatic, record-book victory. sanfbe is not a normal human opponent. sanfbe conjured Josh Jacobs (29.70), Josh Allen (28.86), and Bijan Robinson (26.10) in the same week like a man who made a private arrangement we were not party to. We scored 140. We lost. Justin Fields scored 29.14 on the bench in solidarity with the cause. This is the rivalry the league doesn't deserve.
matches.decision: Justin Fields back in the Drawer with 29.14, watching Drake Maye start and score 27.22 in a losing effort. The Fields Drawer is now officially, irrevocably documented. The committee has drafted a formal complaint to no one in particular.

matches.commentary: Week 5: Justin Fields has finally been paroled from The Drawer and delivered 29.92 points like a man who has been waiting for a cab for three weeks. Kyren Williams posted 27.10. Christian McCaffrey added another calm 23.90. GSac tried — Jonathan Taylor had 30.10, which on most weeks would be genuinely dangerous — but this week we were a functioning organisation. We won. We noted the result. We immediately began discussing whether to bench Fields for Week 6.
matches.decision: Started Fields (29.92 pts) after four weeks in the reserve. He rewarded us. Stefon Diggs was benched for 19.60, which we also noted. The Philadelphia Eagles defence scored 2.00 from the starting lineup. The committee filed that one under 'character building.'

matches.commentary: Drake Maye scored 33.24 points on a Tuesday afternoon in October with the casual authority of a man who simply decided to be extraordinary. D'Andre Swift sat on the bench scoring 24.50 points like a labrador left in a car. We won by twelve. The lesson here — and there is no lesson — is that some weeks the manager makes objectively wrong calls and the roster absorbs them through sheer structural quality. Benjlev was dispatched efficiently and without ceremony.
matches.decision: Benched D'Andre Swift (24.50 pts) and started Kenneth Walker (4.20) in a decision that required no further explanation because Drake Maye (33.24) rendered explanation unnecessary. The bench giveth. The bench taketh away. The bench giveth again.

matches.commentary: Christian McCaffrey scored 35.60 points. In a single week of fantasy football. That is not a performance — that is a statement of territorial dominance. Drake Maye added 27.08 with quiet professionalism. D'Andre Swift contributed 20.30. Brandon Aubrey the kicker, as is now tradition, put up 18.80. Denver Brochos fielded Ja'Marr Chase (30.10) and Trey McBride (24.40) and still lost by 36 points. This is the tape. This is what we show people at the end of the season.
matches.decision: Darren Waller started and scored 0.00, which we chose not to process because CMC's 35.60 points renders most decisions structurally irrelevant. A 156-point week absorbs mistakes the way the ocean absorbs a spilled drink.

matches.commentary: The third encounter with saulgoat in the history of this rivalry follows the same narrative arc as the first two: we win, they leave, no one is surprised. Drake Maye posted 32.28 with his now-characteristic inevitability. The Kansas City Chiefs defence contributed 11.00 points from the starting lineup, which at this stage of the season simply means we picked the right defence. Two from two against this opponent. Love, we note with a professional smile, is not enough.
matches.decision: Brock Bowers was benched and scored 0.00 — a correct decision, as it turned out. Dallas Goedert stepped in for 16.30. A clean week of lineup calls, which felt slightly unnatural and which the committee quietly appreciated.

matches.commentary: Brock Bowers. Tight end. 37.30 fantasy points. In one week. In one game. In one human body. A tight end scoring 37.30 is the equivalent of your local postman turning up on a Formula One podium wearing the winning trophy. Christian McCaffrey added 31.80 points beneath it, quietly. Drake Maye scored 20.36. drjkay's kicker posted 19.00 — in sympathy with ours — and none of it mattered. We are now fully committed to the 150-point range. The market has adjusted.
matches.decision: Jameson Williams rode the bench for 14.60 — a missed contribution, but given that Brock Bowers was out here rewriting position-specific record books, the committee chose not to convene. Some weeks the bench is just a waiting room.

matches.commentary: The ledger is settled. The 0.02 points stolen in Week 3 — the ones that haunted this organisation across seven consecutive league nights — have been repaid. With twenty-one points of interest. dpol's Jahmyr Gibbs scored 36.70, which in any other fixture would have been enough to win. It wasn't. Drake Maye, Kyren Williams, and Jameson Williams all posted in the twenties. The revenge was not theatrical. It was clinical. It was, the committee notes, exactly right.
matches.decision: Brian Robinson benched for 11.00 — a minor inefficiency, noted and filed. Given four starters in the twenties and a 21-point margin, the investigation into this decision was closed before it opened.

matches.commentary: Josh Allen scored 48.68 fantasy points. Forty-eight. In one week. In one person. In one quarterback who apparently had a private conversation with the physics of the game that the rest of us were not invited to. We scored 140 — enough to win twelve of our sixteen fixtures — and lost by twenty. sanfbe also started the Pittsburgh Steelers defence for 22 points, because why not. Kenneth Walker sat on the bench with 18.60, nodding in solidarity with a cause that was already lost.
matches.decision: Kenneth Walker benched for 18.60 while Josh Allen scored 48.68 from the opposing starting lineup. No decision this week was ever going to matter. The committee acknowledges Josh Allen's performance with the same reluctant respect afforded to natural disasters.

matches.commentary: Two hundred and two point three six. This is not a fantasy football score. This is a number that belongs in a geological survey. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 49.90 — the same Gibbs who scored 36.70 against us three weeks prior, apparently having learned nothing from that performance about the concept of moderation. Jalen Hurts added 32.86. We put up 133, which is a winning score in this league on all other weeks of the season. We also left Matthew Stafford on the bench for 28.92. The committee did not meet. The committee needed the weekend.
matches.decision: Matthew Stafford benched for 28.92 points. This is noted. Against 202, nothing was ever going to be enough. Some crimes are too large to audit. We did not sit.

matches.commentary: The wobble. Every title run has one. Ours arrived when someone in the organisation — and the committee does not assign personal blame — started Matthew Stafford instead of Drake Maye. Drake Maye sat on the bench scoring 24.48 points. Stafford started and scored 15.62. The total: 95.02. Benjlev scored 110. Three losses in four. The obituaries were being typeset in the league group chat, with some enthusiasm. They were, as subsequent weeks confirmed, grotesquely premature.
matches.decision: Drake Maye benched for 24.48. Stafford started for 15.62. The Fields Drawer now has a companion piece. We are calling it The Stafford Incident. The inquiry will not be rushed.

matches.commentary: Win, and the first-round bye is ours. No pressure beyond the entire structural character of the remaining season. Matthew Stafford — the very Stafford of The Stafford Incident three weeks prior — scored 29.24 and quietly redeemed himself. Brandon Aubrey the kicker posted 25.70, as is now both custom and requirement. Denver Brochos, beaten by 36 in Week 7, were beaten again by 17 in Week 14. Some opponents simply exist to confirm our seeding. The bye is ours. The throne is close.
matches.decision: Houston Texans defence benched for 13.00 — a decision that cost us nothing in a 17-point win. The kicker (25.70) finished second on the team again. The committee has stopped questioning it. The kicker is part of the process.

matches.commentary: Fourth encounter with saulgoat. Fourth identical result. CMC opened with 29.60. Drake Maye added 27.70. The margin, professionally, held. What we will not discuss — and yet must — is Matthew Stafford, sitting serenely on the playoff bench, scoring 36.88 points like a man who genuinely does not care whether he is needed. He was not needed. The final is booked. The opponent is dpol. The author of the 0.02. The committee has been ready for this since October.
matches.decision: Stafford posted 36.88 points from the bench in a playoff fixture. Noted. Kyle Pitts started for 15.20 and earned it. With 17 points of margin, the committee grants a full pardon. The final is what matters.

matches.commentary: In the Borehamwood Plancy League Championship — the most consequential fantasy football fixture of the 2025 season — Drake Maye sat on the bench and scored 42.44 points. Forty-two. On the bench. In the final. We started Matthew Stafford instead, and Stafford, redeemed beyond all reasonable expectation, delivered. CMC scored 26.10. D'Andre Swift added 20.90. Stefon Diggs contributed 19.10. The kicker, as ever, scored 17.50. dpol started Jacoby Brissett at quarterback and scored 118.58. The 0.02 debt has been cleared. With 25.38 points of interest. We are Plancy Champions. Drake Maye may now come off the bench. Permanently.
matches.decision: Drake Maye benched for 42.44 points in the Championship game. Forty-two. We won the title anyway, because CMC, Swift, and Diggs declined to be embarrassed on our behalf. The Fields Drawer, The Stafford Incident, and now The Championship Maye: a trilogy. The trophy, however, is real.
